title: Emergency capacity bridging and postmortem for dedicated fleet scaling regression
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Summary: On 2025-02-10 at ~09:12 UTC a regression in the dedicated-pool autoscaler logic caused delayed scale-ups for multiple customer reserved pools. The resulting headroom deficit produced elevated 95/99 latency and failed requests for a subset of dedicated customers for ~72 minutes. This ticket captures the emergency bridging actions, root cause analysis, telemetry fixes, and prioritized action items for long-term prevention.
timeline: 2025-02-10 09:12 UTC: Pager triggered - dedicated-pool headroom alarm (region: us-west-2)
2025-02-10 09:16 UTC: On-call verified increased queue length & token throttles visible on Console route dashboard (link in artifacts)
2025-02-10 09:25 UTC: Emergency manual headroom injection: ops increased reserved burst capacity for 3 impacted pools to buy time
2025-02-10 09:38 UTC: Autoscaler service logs show backpressure loop - leader lease renewal jitter + misapplied smoothing window prevented scale out decision
2025-02-10 09:45 UTC: Temporary per-tenant throttling policy applied to reduce token churn for the largest noisy tenant
2025-02-10 10:02 UTC: Canary rollback of autoscaler deploy from 2025-02-09 21:10 (roll-forward later after hotfix)
2025-02-10 10:24 UTC: Activated fallback routing to compatible smaller model variant for latency sensitive routes; shards rebalanced
2025-02-10 11:05 UTC: Traffic stabilized; error rates returned to baseline after autoscaler hotfix and headroom injection
2025-02-10 11:20 UTC: Post-incident coordination call scheduled; customer outreach initiated for impacted accounts
root_cause_summary: A change in the autoscaler smoothing algorithm (introduced in runtime-1.22 candidate) modified the effective responsiveness to sudden queue growth. Combined with a leader election jitter regression and a recent KV cache eviction change that temporarily increased memory churn, the autoscaler missed scaling windows for ~6 contiguous intervals. The orchestration layer’s fallback thresholds were too permissive, delaying fallback to burst capacity and alternative model variants.
mitigations_applied: Manual burst quota increase for affected dedicated pools
Rollback of autoscaler candidate and redeploy stable version with emergency patch
Applied per-tenant temporary throttling for the top noisy customer to protect shared pool headroom
Enabled earlier fallback to pre-configured compatible model variant (lower-latency) on overloaded routes
Restarted leader-election service with reduced jitter settings and tightened lease timeouts
Short-term KV cache eviction tuning to reduce memory churn during scale events
impact_metrics: Peak 95th percentile latency: +420ms above baseline for affected pools
Error rate spike: 6.8% failed requests for dedicated routes during incident window
Duration: 72 minutes from alert to full remediation on all pools
Number of impacted customers: 7 reserved accounts (3 high-traffic tenants)
Estimated cost of emergency burst: $2.7k additional cloud GPU hours
postmortem_notes: Root cause involves interplay between three independently-reviewed changes (autoscaler smoothing, leader election jitter, KV cache eviction policy) — regression passed unit tests but failed integration at production scale
Alerting gap: our headroom alarm threshold fired but runbook escalation lagged because the on-call page contained an outdated escalation matrix
Fallback behavior: existing fallback to smaller model variants exists but thresholds were set conservatively and need to be per-route and per-tenant adaptive
Telemetry: missing explicit metric for consecutive missed scale windows; added new metric in follow-ups
Customer communication: support sent targeted notifications and offered SLA credit where appropriate; engineering provided timeline and remediation summary
review_and_feedback: PM review (Anika Shah): request to add customer-facing summary for the next status update
Design review (Rui Chen): suggested clearer Console indicator for 'fallback active' state to reduce on-call cognitive load
SRE review (Omar Patel): recommended runbook rewrite to include step-by-step commands for manual headroom injection and validation queries
Security review: no data exfiltration observed; confirmed by security lead (Lena Becker)
action_items: AI-1: Add integration test that simulates fast ramp of concurrent requests and validates autoscaler reacts within expected windows (owner: Jun Park, estimate: 5)
AI-2: Implement per-tenant minimum reserved headroom toggle and expose in Dedicated Console (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 8)
AI-3: Shorten leader lease/heartbeat defaults and add canary to leader-election service (owner: Diego Ramos, estimate: 3)
AI-4: Introduce metric 'consecutive_scale_misses' and wire to PagerDuty with lower threshold (owner: Maya Alvarez, estimate: 2)
AI-5: Update runbook and escalation matrix; add quick run section for emergency burst (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2)
AI-6: Make fallback thresholds adaptive by route/customer profile; prototype in runtime-1.23 canary (owner: Research/Applied ML, estimate: 8)
AI-7: Post-deploy checklist: automated smoke with synthetic traffic for 10 minutes after autoscaler changes (owner: Platform CI, estimate: 3)
AI-8: Customer remediation: outreach and SLA credit proposals for impacted accounts (owner: Support, estimate: 1)
AI-9: Document lessons learned and cross-team readout scheduled (owner: Maya Alvarez, estimate: 1, due: 2025-03-09)
next_steps: Prioritize AI-1, AI-3, AI-4 for the upcoming sprint; block merge of further autoscaler smoothing changes until canary validated
Schedule cross-functional tabletop drill for 'dedicated pool headroom' scenario in Cycle 43
Bundle per-tenant headroom and adaptive fallback into runtime-1.23 milestone and measure cost/latency trade-offs in lab environment
Publish public postmortem summary for affected customers and update knowledge base article
